messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@sandstonellabs.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sandstone Labs — initial interop scope (LangChain / LlamaIndex)

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. Sandstone Labs is moving to a hybrid model for customers and we'd like Redwood to be a first-class runtime option for our LangChain and LlamaIndex bundles. Before we schedule a longer technical deep-dive, can you confirm the following high-level items so we can scope our internal workstreams?

1) Tracing hooks: do you expose a lightweight trace callback (token-level or call-level) we can connect to our telemetry so customers see per-request attribution? If so, what format and auth?
2) Embedding shim: we want a standardized shim so LlamaIndex can persist vectors to Redwood's embedding endpoint without requiring bespoke adapter code. Any recommended contract or sample?
3) Acceptance tests: what does Redwood expect for an interoperability acceptance test (latency SLOs, token attribution, KV cache behavior)?
4) Commercial: do you require an ISV agreement or a developer partner addendum to list Sandstone as an approved integration partner?

Attaching our short spec (sandstone-sdk-interop-spec.pdf) to give context.

Would appreciate a short reply to the bullets and a suggested time for a 45-minute tech sync next week.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Integrations | Sandstone Labs
elena.ruiz@sandstonellabs.com
+1 415-555-0182

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sandstone Labs — initial interop scope (LangChain / LlamaIndex)

Elena — thanks for the clear spec and the ask. Looping in Marissa (ISV partnerships), Vanessa (platform integration), and Jordan (runtime-side dev) so we can give concrete answers and propose an acceptance checklist.

Quick replies inline below:  

> 1) Tracing hooks: do you expose a lightweight trace callback (token-level or call-level) we can connect to our telemetry so customers see per-request attribution? If so, what format and auth?

We provide call-level tracing in the public API and can emit token-level deltas when customers enable "detailed attribution" on a per-project basis. Auth is via scoped API keys; hub-style webhook delivery is supported for partners. Jordan will add details on payloads.

> 2) Embedding shim: we want a standardized shim so LlamaIndex can persist vectors to Redwood's embedding endpoint without requiring bespoke adapter code. Any recommended contract or sample?

Yes — we have a recommended shim pattern (REST contract + line-delimited NDJSON) and a tiny reference repo we can share. Attaching an initial checklist we use for partner onboarding.

> 3) Acceptance tests: what does Redwood expect for an interoperability acceptance test (latency SLOs, token attribution, KV cache behavior)?

We typically validate: 1) 95th-token latency under 200ms for short-chat profiles, 2) consistent token attribution for >=99% of traced requests in the smoke set, 3) KV cache warm-start behavior for context preservation across chains. Marissa will propose a formal checklist.

> 4) Commercial: do you require an ISV agreement or a developer partner addendum to list Sandstone as an approved integration partner?

Yes, for co-marketing and partner listing we sign a standard ISV partner addendum; for anything with revenue share we use a simple SOW. Legal will follow up once we have a scoped pilot.

I'll schedule a 45-minute slot Tue/Wed for the tech sync — Marissa, Vanessa, Jordan, please propose windows.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-initial-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 12KB)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sandstone Labs — initial interop scope (LangChain / LlamaIndex)

Neha — thanks for the loop. Short internal plan below (action items + owners).

Summary / owners:
- Technical contract & payloads (Jordan): draft token-level and call-level trace payloads; include minimal headers + attribution fields; target: API contract doc v0.1.
- Embedding shim sample (Vanessa): produce an NDJSON shim example and a tiny Python adapter for LlamaIndex that calls Redwood's embeddings endpoint. Include authentication snippet for partner keys.
- Acceptance checklist (Marissa): formalize the test vectors (10 sample prompts, 3 synthetic chaining scenarios), define pass/fail gating for pilot.
- Legal/commercial (Neha): draft ISV addendum & partner listing terms; propose pilot terms (1 month, free eval credits).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
* Performance: 95th-token latency < 200ms on our shared dev pool for the smoke prompts.
* Attribution: token-level attributions present for >=99% of test calls when enabled.
* Functional: embedding shim accepts NDJSON upload and returns vector ids within 2s on average.

Deliverables and timeline (proposal):
- 1 week: Jordan produces API contract v0.1 and sample payloads.
- 1 week: Vanessa delivers shim sample + Python adapter.
- 10 business days: Marissa publishes acceptance checklist and test vectors.
- End of pilot (4 weeks from start): joint validation run and postmortem.

I've attached a short runbook that codifies our usual partner onboarding steps. Jordan & Vanessa — if you can start on the sample artifacts this week we can hit the timelines.

—Marissa
Director, ISV Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

- Tracing: our telemetry team prefers token-delta push webhooks (HMAC-signed) vs polling. If Redwood can support HMAC-signed webhooks in the partner key model, that's ideal.
